Keyword(s): BGP Monitoring, BMP, Streaming Telemetry, Route Anomaly Detection, Real‑Time Network Analytics.
Abstract: The Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) plays a critical role in inter-domain routing across the Internet, yet it lacks native support for real-time monitoring and anomaly detection.
This limitation exposes networks to risks such as prefix hijacking, route leaks, and misconfigurations that can severely impact routing integrity.
Traditional monitoring solutions like SNMP polling and log-based analysis fail to capture the dynamic nature of BGP events due to their reactive approach and limited granularity.
To address these challenges, this paper presents a real-time BGP monitoring system that integrates the BGP Monitoring Protocol (BMP) with streaming telemetry.

BMP enables routers to export unfiltered pre-RIB updates, offering deep visibility into all route advertisements and withdrawals, while telemetry facilitates low-latency, push-based data transport to centralized processing systems.

The proposed architecture leverages a modular pipeline built with open-source tools including Kafka for scalable message brokering, InfluxDB for high-performance time-series storage, and Grafana for real-time visualization.

Open Access is an initiative that aims to make scientific research freely available to all.
It’s based on principles of collaboration, unobstructed discovery, and, most importantly, scientific progression.
As PhD students, we found it difficult to access the research we needed, so we decided to create a new Open Access publisher that levels the playing field for scientists across the world.
By making research easy to access, and puts the academic needs of the researchers before the business interests of publishers.

Authors, Editors and Institutions We are a community of more than 103,000 authors and editors from 3,291 institutions spanning 160 countries, including Nobel Prize winners and some of the world’s most-cited researchers.
Publishing on IntechOpen allows authors to earn citations and find new collaborators, meaning more people see your work not only from your own field of study, but from other related fields too.
